correctness.rationale: A=[[0,1],[1,1]] has determinant -1. The exact matrices (A^3-I)/2, (A^6-I)/4 and (A^12-I)/8 have odd determinants. Primitive 2-adic states therefore have respective least periods 3,6,3·2^(j-1) for j>=3; the squaring/odd-multiplier induction proves no earlier return at every 2-adic layer. Each primitive layer has 3·2^(2j-2) states, and modulo 3 the only cycles have length 1 (zero) and 8 (all nonzero). CRT pairs an r-cycle and s-cycle into gcd(r,s) orbits of lcm(r,s). Assembling gives k=3 multiplicities (1,1,2,1,4,21), k>=4 (1,1,2,1,4,93) plus 9·2^(j-1) at length 3·2^(j-1) for j=5..k; total 9·2^k−42. Independent direct enumeration of all (3·2^k)^2 state pairs for k=3,4,5,6 gave 30,102,246,534 orbits with every length/count matched. The induction, not finite testing, establishes all k>=3.
residual_risks: Only modulus m=3·2^k with k>=3; no claim for other OEIS conjectures.
